question: What is the basic structural and functional unit of the human body?
explanation: Cells are recognized universally as the fundamental building blocks that make up all living tissues and structures in the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h1)

question: An organ is best defined as a structure composed of what components?

options.B: Two or more different tissue types working together
options.C: A single uniform layer of specialized epithelial cells
options.D: Independent atoms bonded together by chemical forces

explanation: Organs require a combination of diverse tissues, such as epithelial and muscle tissue, to execute complex physiological duties. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h1)

question: The primary physiological function of the kidneys is to do what?

options.A: Pump oxygenated blood to peripheral skeletal muscles
options.B: Filter metabolic waste and regulate body fluids
options.C: Synthesize digestive enzymes and store excess glucose
options.D: Exchange respiratory gases across alveolar membranes

explanation: Kidneys process blood to clear out toxins and manage fluid and electrolyte balance via urine production. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h2)

question: A patient with severe liver failure will most directly experience impairment in which bodily process?

options.A: Filtration of cellular debris from cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: Direct electrical conduction to cardiac muscle fibers
options.D: Exchange of carbon dioxide within the pleural cavity

explanation: The liver is uniquely responsible for metabolizing toxins and manufacturing bile necessary for normal digestion. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h2)

question: Which organ system is primarily responsible for rapid communication and control in the body?
explanation: The nervous system uses electrical signals and neurotransmitters to coordinate immediate responses to internal and external stimuli. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which system works alongside the urinary system to regulate blood pH and fluid balance?
explanation: Blood circulation connects the kidneys and lungs to the rest of the body, allowing continuous monitoring and adjustment of fluid and acid-base balance. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h3)

question: Homeostasis is best defined as what physiological state?

options.A: An unchanging external environment surrounding the human body
options.B: A complete absence of metabolic activity within body tissues
options.C: A stable internal environment maintained despite external changes
options.D: A rapid fluctuation of vital signs during physical exertion

explanation: Homeostasis represents the dynamic equilibrium the body maintains to keep internal conditions compatible with life. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why must multiple organ systems cooperate to maintain normal blood pressure?

options.A: Control relies on rapid neural signals, cardiac output, and fluid volume regulation
options.B: Blood pressure is managed exclusively by hormonal output from the endocrine pancreas
options.C: Skeletal muscles contract continuously to maintain resting vascular resistance
options.D: Digestive organs dictate systemic blood flow distribution during rest

explanation: Blood pressure stability requires the combined efforts of the nervous system for speed, the heart for pumping force, and the kidneys for fluid control. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h4)

question: A patient with impaired kidney function is prescribed a medication cleared through the urinary system. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Switch the medication route from oral to intravenous administration
options.B: Encourage the patient to hold all fluids to rest the kidneys
options.C: Verify renal lab results before administering the ordered dose
options.D: Administer the medication as ordered without checking lab values

explanation: Reduced kidney function delays drug excretion, increasing toxicity risks unless the nurse checks labs and collaborates with the prescriber for dose adjustments. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h5)

question: Why should a nurse assess multiple body systems when a patient reports a single localized complaint?

options.A: Organ systems are interdependent, so localized issues often impact other systems
options.B: Localized symptoms never accurately reflect the true source of pathology
options.C: Hospital protocol requires a full head-to-toe assessment for every minor symptom
options.D: Patients frequently exaggerate localized pain to gain attention

explanation: Because body systems rely on each other, a problem in one area quickly triggers compensatory responses or secondary failures elsewhere. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h5)
